title: feat(missions): missions are governed Runtime records with an enforced lifecycle (MS-1, ADR-0044)

sourceMetadata.subject: feat(missions): missions are governed Runtime records with an enforced lifecycle (MS-1, ADR-0044)
sourceMetadata.body:
Implements ADR-0044 Decisions 1 and 2. A mission (MS-YYYY-NNNN) is a committed record in runtime/executive/missions carrying the approved Mission System structure: objective, type, priority, owner (always the Chief Agent), proposer, participants, repositories, services, approvals, risks, a plan of epics and tasks with acceptance criteria, validation plan, linked commits, recovery anchor, produced knowledge and history. The lifecycle is enforced with authority by step: the Chief Agent or the owner creates, plans and submits; only the owner approves, rejects, blocks, unblocks, cancels and archives, with a reason where it matters; executing, validating, completed and knowledge extracted are system steps on evidence (MS-2, MS-4). Every transition is recorded with actor, time and reason. Owner steps are on the human-only executive route list, so agents are refused at the boundary as well as by the lifecycle. Verified live: the Chief Agent created and submitted MS-2026-0001, its approval attempt and an agent posing as human were refused, the owner's approval was recorded; runtime suites 674/674.
